input.summary: The new batch contract is not implemented consistently: PostgreSQL silently commits partial batches, and the reaper still calls the removed single-record API. The retry helper also does not retry.

findings.title: put_many violates the all-or-nothing contract
findings.description: The implementation catches duplicate-key conflicts and continues processing later records, then commits the successful writes. This can leave a partially persisted batch while returning normally, directly contradicting Store's documented atomicity contract and causing callers to report the whole batch as accepted.
findings.recommendation: Abort the transaction and raise StoreError on the first conflict (or any write failure), allowing the transaction context to roll back all writes; remove the continue path and unused counter.

findings.title: Reaper still calls the removed single-record store method
findings.description: Store's interface was changed from put to put_many, but sweep continues to invoke put. With the updated Store implementations this raises AttributeError instead of reaping any expired job.
findings.recommendation: Build records for the expired jobs and call put_many, or otherwise update the reaper to use the new batch API.

findings.title: sweep_with_retry never retries
findings.description: Despite its name and attempt parameter, this method catches an exception, sleeps once, and immediately re-raises it. A caller using this helper still gets no retry attempt, so transient store failures are not recovered.
findings.recommendation: Retry sweep in a bounded loop, incrementing the attempt between failures and returning on success; only re-raise after the configured retry limit.

findings.title: Duplicate keys no longer produce StoreError
findings.description: The API explicitly translates StoreError into HTTP 409, but put_many swallows _Conflict and returns successfully. Duplicate records therefore can be reported as accepted even though they were not written.
findings.recommendation: Translate _Conflict into StoreError (including the conflicting key) instead of continuing, and roll back the complete batch.
